method: Deterministic, zero-AI-cost replay. Real Riot source text (tests/fixtures/unseen-packages/riot-2025-2026-credit-facility/extracted-text, unchanged/frozen) run through the CURRENT (post-Unit-B) buildPackageGraph -> classifyPackageDocuments/extractPackageDocumentIdentities/resolvePackageRelationships -> runAmendmentPipeline -> computeOperativeDocument production functions, unmodified from the committed code at HEAD (41ab563). No ground truth re-adjudicated, no thresholds altered, no Riot-specific code paths added or exercised.

docBTarget.result: doc-b's RESTATES reference resolves to doc-c (INCORRECT - the true target is doc-a), status REVIEW_REQUIRED, confidence 0.55, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_ONLY_MATCH.
docBTarget.rootCauseOfIncorrectTarget: NOT a Unit B1/B2 defect. Unit B1's regex fix correctly detects doc-b's recital reference ('The Borrower and Lender are parties to a Credit Agreement dated as of April 22, 2025') - this is the exact real-world recital-style gap Unit B1 was built to close, and it now fires correctly (previously DETERMINISTIC_NO_SIGNAL - zero references detected at all under the old regex). The wrong target arises from a SEPARATE, pre-existing, out-of-scope defect in document-classifier.ts: doc-a's real text is classified as COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE (confidence 0.9, DETERMINISTIC_TITLE_PATTERN, evidence 'Compliance Certificate') rather than CREDIT_AGREEMENT, because doc-a's own table of contents/Exhibit E lists a 'Form of Compliance Certificate' that the classifier's title-pattern search matches ahead of doc-a's real 'CREDIT AGREEMENT' title. With doc-a excluded from the CREDIT_AGREEMENT/AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT type family, resolveAgreementReference's direct-date-match step finds no candidate (doc-a doesn't qualify), and its type-only-match fallback incorrectly lands on doc-c (the only remaining type match) at capped confidence 0.55/REVIEW_REQUIRED - never a false-confident RESOLVED.
docBTarget.verifiedIndependently: Confirmed by running classifyPackageDocuments directly against doc-a's real frozen source text with the current, unmodified document-classifier.ts - the COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE misclassification is reproducible and pre-existing, not introduced by this remediation.

docCTarget.result: doc-c's RESTATES reference resolves to doc-b (CORRECT), status REVIEW_REQUIRED, confidence 0.7, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_CHRONOLOGICAL_PREDECESSOR.
docCTarget.significance: This is Unit B2's date-ambiguity safeguard working exactly as designed on the real Riot evidence: doc-c's own recital quotes the ORIGINAL April 22, 2025 date (doc-a's date) qualified by 'as amended and restated as of the First Amendment and Restatement Effective Date' - the generic superseding-qualifier phrase. Rather than directly (and wrongly) matching doc-a by that quoted date, the chronological-predecessor fallback correctly identifies doc-b (May 19, 2025 - the most recent same-type document dated before doc-c's own April 21, 2026 execution date) as the true immediate predecessor. Correctly capped at REVIEW_REQUIRED/0.7 confidence - never falsely confident.

operativeDocumentResult.allThreeBaseDocuments: REVIEW_REQUIRED (cycle) for doc-b and doc-c as base; NOT_APPLICABLE for doc-a as base (doc-a is not part of the resolved restatement graph, since neither resolved RESTATES edge names doc-a as predecessor or successor).
operativeDocumentResult.reviewReason: The restatement relationships resolved for this instrument form a cycle - doc-b's effect names doc-c as its restated predecessor, and doc-c's effect names doc-b as ITS restated predecessor, so neither is ever the un-superseded end of the chain.
operativeDocumentResult.safetyAssessment: This is the CORRECT, safe outcome given the corrupted input the document-classifier defect produces. computeOperativeDocument's cycle-detection safeguard (Unit B4) correctly refuses to designate either document as operative rather than guessing - no document is ever confidently asserted as currently governing. This demonstrates the safeguard functioning exactly as designed under a genuine (if unrelated) real-world data-quality problem, not a defect in Unit B's own logic.
operativeDocumentResult.deletedCarveOutImplication: Since no document is ever confidently designated operative, the deleted-carve-out safety requirement (historical/deleted language must never become current trusted truth) is trivially satisfied here: nothing is asserted current at all, so nothing superseded can be mistaken for it.

notInScopeDisclosure: The document-classifier.ts misclassification of doc-a is a genuine, real, pre-existing defect discovered as a byproduct of this replay. It is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this remediation's two authorized units (Unit A: semantic-compiler definitions; Unit B: package-graph restatement-target resolution + operative-document concept) and was NOT fixed here, per the mission's explicit prohibition on scope creep and package-specific tuning. It should be raised as a candidate finding for a future, separately-scoped architecture decision - not patched inside this session.
